plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a twist: the winner pays the second-highest bid. This is a Vickrey auction variant. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding less risks losing a profitable opportunity, and bidding more risks winning but paying more than your value if the second-highest bid is higher than your value. Since this is the first round and there's no history to learn from, I will bid my true value.

I need to maximize my profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, I want to bid as high as possible to win, but not so high that my profit is negative. My value is $34. I will bid slightly above what I anticipate the other bidders might bid, while ensuring I still make a profit. Given the value range of $0-$49, and that other bidders are rational, they will likely bid below their value. I will bid slightly below my value to ensure a positive profit if I win, but high enough to be competitive.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. I will bid my value of $33.
